solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Play Switzerland, say, neutral by design

parts.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

indicators.note: something done by design is deliberately arranged, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as part of the fodder
taken as written, as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A country famous for staying out of wars is described as neutral on purpose, as a matter of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' leads you to read Switzerland as a sports opponent, but it gives the vehicle code. 'by design' scrambles the fodder 'say' plus 'neutral'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandon Thomas's 1892 farce about an undergraduate impersonating a rich aunt is a famous stage comedy.

clue.text: Screen copper's preliminary review of Scottish town

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the preliminary part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Tain is a small town in the Scottish Highlands, on the Dornoch Firth

explanation.surface: A policeman gives an initial assessment of a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal; Tain is a Highland town.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape hung across a window or stage serves to screen what lies behind it.

clue.text: Nourishment for insect ingesting fruit

indicators.note: an insect ingesting something takes it inside itself, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: an ant is a common insect
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A bug feeds by eating a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for food or sustenance, the source of the word alimentary.

clue.text: Fabulous but scandalous green lady

indicators.note: scandalous behaviour is shocking and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone inexperienced is wonderful yet disgraceful at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous in its root sense means belonging to fable or myth, the stuff of legend.

clue.text: After jetty ends, look out! German removing faulty gun from boat

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
removing takes the stated letters out of the longer word

parts.note: Achtung is the German warning cry meaning look out
a faulty gun is one out of order, so the three letters of gun appear scrambled as they sit at the end of the German word

explanation.surface: At the end of a pier a German shouts a warning and disarms a defective weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The German warning cry ends in letters that are a jumble of 'gun', so 'removing' that faulty gun leaves the German number eight, which follows the last letter of 'jetty'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing or motor vessel used for pleasure cruising or racing is a kind of boat.

clue.text: One wondering what it's like to be funny

parts.note: a means one, as in a single item
to muse is to ponder or wonder, so musing is wondering

explanation.surface: Someone asks themselves what it feels like to be comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what it's like to be' simply links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comic or entertaining enough to raise a smile is described as funny.

clue.text: Family boys with reports about Joseph? Not half!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: news consists of reports of events

indicators.note: not half means losing half of the word, here its first three letters

explanation.surface: Boys in a family hear accounts about a man named Joseph, and the exclamation means very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much'. Here it keeps only the back half of Joseph, which 'about' then puts into the reports.
explanation.definitionFit: The sons of one's brother or sister are male relatives, boys within the family.

clue.text: Play! Bowled by agile character

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
lithe means supple or agile
spirit is a person's character or temperament

explanation.surface: A cricketer is dismissed by a nimble player while someone urges playing on.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward's 1941 comedy about a ghostly first wife is a well-known stage work.

clue.text: Mad to get a new top when having fun

indicators.note: getting a new top means the opening letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: barking, short for barking mad, is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy over a fresh shirt while enjoying themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: BARKING (British slang for crazy) has its first letter replaced by L.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is to play pranks or fool around, so this means playing and enjoying oneself.

clue.text: Cake? Ask for a tiny piece, darling

indicators.note: asking for something is said out loud, so the request is heard rather than read

parts.note: a crumb is a tiny piece and pet is a term of endearment for a darling, so the request is crumb, pet

explanation.surface: At tea, someone asks a loved one to spare just a morsel of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying 'crumb, pet' gives the answer's sound; the query on 'Cake?' admits it is a griddle bread rather than a true cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft round griddle bread eaten toasted with butter at teatime is loosely counted among cakes in Britain.

clue.text: Play Guardian?

definitions.meaning: a drama by Harold Pinter, first staged in 1960
a guardian or custodian of a building, with the query hinting at The Guardian, a British newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: Pinter's play takes its title from the custodian figure, and a caretaker looks after property as its keeper.

clue.text: Part-payment for something horse-trader has within

indicators.note: the hyphenated word has the needed letters held inside it, so the rest of it is discarded

parts.note: a horse-trader carries out a trade, the word sitting inside the compound
within means in

explanation.surface: A dealer in horses keeps something inside as part of a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger thought it clumsy that the business word sits inside 'horse-trader' while 'within' also has to supply the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: An old item handed over to reduce the price of a new purchase serves as partial payment.

clue.text: Initially tactless French laugh at yours truly's craft

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: rire is the French verb to laugh
yours truly is a jocular way of saying me, the speaker

explanation.surface: Someone tactless and French mocks the writer's handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill but means a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek or Roman warship with three banks of oars is a seagoing vessel.

clue.text: Painter of the modern style

indicators.note: the letters are part of the words that follow, held within them

explanation.surface: An artist working in a contemporary manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born surrealist artist known for collage and frottage.

clue.text: Take time away from East Anglia to review pain relief

indicators.note: reviewing something means going over it again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
taking a letter away removes it from the longer name
away from names the place the letter is removed from

explanation.surface: Remove the clock from a region of England and rethink how pain is treated.
explanation.walkthrough: East Anglia is the eastern English region of Norfolk and Suffolk. 'Take ... away from' leaves EASANGLIA, which 'to review' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the medical term for the absence or easing of pain, as provided by painkillers.

clue.text: Not ceased making up stories

indicators.note: making up means composing, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has not stopped inventing tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Short amusing or interesting accounts of real incidents are told as tales.

clue.text: Convert experts to see Terence is gutted

parts.note: pros are professionals, experts
a see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is a cathedral city with its own see

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A newly converted believer asks specialists to visit Terence, who is devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like British slang for upset but means emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: A proselyte is a person who has converted to a new religion or belief.

clue.text: Bird wins the heart of disciple; that's preposterous

indicators.note: the heart of a word is what is left once its outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: an apostle is a disciple, one of the twelve followers of Christ
that's rich is an ironic exclamation meaning that's absurd

explanation.surface: A bird wins over a follower's affections, which is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the heart of' strips AP and LE from APOSTLE to leave OST; 'wins' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless African bird is the biggest living bird species.

clue.text: Learned simple English first, one having time inside

indicators.note: first puts this letter at the front of the answer
inside puts the pair within the other word

parts.note: rude can mean primitive or simple, as in rude huts

indicators.note: having joins one letter directly to the next

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A beginner learns basic English first, with one person given time to study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts E at the front; 'inside' puts IT into RUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudite describes someone of great scholarship, widely read and knowledgeable.

clue.text: Point at which to put on apron

definitions.meaning: a point or phase in a process
to put on a play is to mount it before an audience
the apron is the part of a theatre's platform in front of the curtain

explanation.surface: The moment when one should tie on a kitchen pinafore.
explanation.definitionFit: A phase in a process, the verb for presenting a show, and a theatre's raised platform all share one word.

clue.text: Repository used by shop endlessly over the years

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second
endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a store is a shop
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: A storeroom used by a shop without interruption for years.
explanation.definitionFit: A repository is a place where things are kept, a depot or warehouse.

clue.text: Images of Ms Gardner, star in the making

parts.note: Ava Gardner was a Hollywood film actress

indicators.note: something in the making is still being formed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pictures of Ava Gardner as a film star still being created.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatars are icons or figures representing a person online, so they are images.

clue.text: About to kiss and make it better

parts.note: re means about or concerning
in snooker or billiards a kiss is a light touch between balls

explanation.surface: Someone about to kiss and make up after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'and' are link words; 'kiss and make up' is the surface's red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Retouching a picture or paintwork improves it with small corrections.

clue.text: Painter left in student accommodation

indicators.note: in places one letter within the painter's name

parts.note: Frans Hals was a Dutch Golden Age portraitist

explanation.surface: An artist has been left in a university residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Halls of residence are British university dormitories.
explanation.definitionFit: Halls of residence are buildings where university students live, often shortened in Britain.

clue.text: Light show has one taken in by girl to a degree

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the other word

parts.note: Dora is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral for one
an MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A light show has someone fooled by a girl to some extent.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama was a nineteenth-century spectacle of painted scenes transformed by changing light.

clue.text: Inconsequential number involved in action

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit, which may go to trial
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An insignificant digit has a part in some activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' is the legal sense, a case brought to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of little importance or significance is trivial.

clue.text: Support accountant getting in with cook's final offering

definitions.text: Support accountant getting in with cook's final offering

indicators.note: getting in means entering inside the other word

parts.note: a tee is a peg that supports a golf ball
ACA is Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants

indicators.note: final picks out the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A golfing accountant arrives just as the cook brings out the last dish at tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' is a golf tee. 'getting in' puts the accountant and the last letter of 'cook's' inside it, and the whole clue also pictures the last treat served at tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, sweet yeast bun with dried fruit, eaten toasted, is a classic British tea offering.

clue.text: Play with Charlotte, Emily and Anne

definitions.meaning: a drama by Anton Chekhov, first staged in 1901
the Brontës, three novelist siblings from Yorkshire

explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's drama is titled for three siblings, and the Brontës were a famous trio of female siblings.
